## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | Ontology operations identify their own canonical store and change boundary; creating, retrieving, or publishing ontology content does not create or activate a Task, alter role ownership, or merge canonical stores. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | Operations reject unresolved, mismatched, or unspecialized project identity; path resolution prevents traversal or symlink escape into sibling projects or unselected filesystem locations., Two projects with the same labels retain separate identities and lookup results. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | A root query does not open a child project's ontology solely because it is under Projects/ or registered; child ontology changes do not silently change root results., Registry-derived representations identify their registry source and do not authorize writes to the represented project. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | The supported JSON-LD profile and local context define record keys and their meanings; ordinary canonical parsing uses Python 3.12 standard-library JSON support., Wiki pages, graph files, indexes, exports, and external tools are not alternative editable sources of canonical ontology facts., ontology.yaml follows the project's documented JSON subset of YAML without introducing a core parser dependency. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | A record containing an HTTP context, an untrusted context, or an escaping file reference is rejected without network access or reading the target., Core parsing does not advertise support for unrestricted JSON-LD processing; unsupported profile features receive an explicit diagnostic. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Two builds from identical ontology, configuration, referenced input bytes, module versions, and generator version produce byte-equivalent generated output., Removing a generated projection loses no canonical knowledge; an explicit rebuild restores it and reports its input versions and digests., compile and build-wiki modify only their declared generated destinations; failed input validation does not publish an apparently successful build or overwrite unrelated files., Approval records, publication receipts, and accepted recovery state are durable records and are not classified or deleted as rebuildable projections. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | The core covers Project, ProjectTemplate, Artifact, Source, Specification, Requirement, Task, TRD, ImplementationPlan, Verification, Evidence, Agent, Role, Skill, Capability, ActionType, MemoryRecord, Lesson, Decision, OntologyConcept, Authority, and Scope, plus terms needed by the competency questions., Concepts model meaning, capability, and relationships; a filesystem location is represented as an artifact binding rather than substituted for the concept., Product-domain vocabulary and root-specific instances are absent from the reusable core. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | Missing modules or a digest/version mismatch produce a precise diagnostic and cannot be treated as a valid current import., A newer depot module does not silently replace a project's selected imported version. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | A project-local subtype or distinct concept can extend the selected core; an attempted incompatible redefinition of a core ID is rejected., Project extensions remain local and do not automatically modify sys4ai-core or another project's ontology. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | Moving a bound artifact or changing a display label preserves the entity ID and existing references., Imported core identities remain stable across projects; project-specific identities are unambiguous across project namespaces., An identifier is not recycled for a different meaning. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | An approved concept with missing required metadata is invalid; a concept with supported optional explanatory fields retains them through reading and wiki generation., Aliases resolve to the underlying stable identity rather than creating accidental duplicate concepts. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | term Task and term TRD return distinct definitions, stable IDs, relevant distinctions, and current source references., Agent-facing answers do not equate document approval with Task activation or implementation completion, or verification with validation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | The type Skill is distinguishable from the installed memory skill instance and the SKILL.md artifact that describes it; type and instance queries preserve that distinction. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | A relationship has a registered predicate and typed endpoints; incoming and outgoing directions remain distinguishable., Configured cardinality and qualifiers survive read/build operations, and invalid endpoint types or cardinalities fail validation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-015` | Retrieval, graph projections, and wiki output identify the kind and source of each included fact., Representing an inferred-fact category does not enable an inference engine or allow derived memory links to redefine canonical concepts. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-016` | Bindings may point to selected SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, ROLE.md, SPECS.md, .agents/skills/, Roles/, and depot/projects.json content within the established project policy., Unselected child content, credentials, secrets, private runtime data, environments, and caches are excluded; tests show that traversal and symlink references cannot bypass the binding policy., Ontology binding setup leaves memory corpus configuration and exclusion rules unchanged. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-017` | A reviewer can resolve a returned definition to its recorded local source version and locator., Changed, missing, or inaccessible source bytes are reported as stale or unavailable and cannot be presented as freshly verified current authority., Validation and build results expose source/configuration/module/helper versions and hashes sufficient to reproduce their reported result. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-018` | Resolving a capability, reading an action type, or validating an ontology does not invoke a skill or grant Task, role, tool, write, publication, or execution authority., When a retrieved definition conflicts with current governing sources, the response identifies the discrepancy and uses those sources for operational rules., ActionType may be described as vocabulary; installing execution interception or semantic pre-execution gates is excluded from this release. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-019` | The writer supplies the exact reviewed change, reason, expected current digest, and applicable authority; stale content, missing authority, an ordinary child actor, or conflicting manager ownership prevents publication., An authorized operation records what actually committed, preserves unrelated bytes, and exposes an exact receipt and bounded recovery result if publication is partial., Ontology uses its own publication path and authority scope; possession of a memory publication grant alone does not authorize ontology writes. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-020` | A deprecated ID remains resolvable with its deprecation reason and replacement when present; old references retain their historical meaning., A changed definition cannot claim approval of the old bytes, and replacing a concept does not recycle its ID or silently rewrite history. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-021` | A suggestion or captured memory remains a proposal and cannot appear as an approved canonical definition without the required publication operation., Rejected proposals and ambiguous extracted links do not silently change approved lookup results. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-022` | Negative examples with a duplicate ID or unresolved relationship target fail with the offending ID and record location; equivalent valid examples pass. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-023` | An unmodeled collision fails validation; an explicitly modeled collision returns the candidate IDs and their distinctions rather than claiming an exact unambiguous resolution. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-024` | Focused invalid examples for each configured constraint fail with actionable diagnostics; strict-specialization cycles fail while a cycle in a relation not declared acyclic is not rejected solely for being a cycle., Validation is deterministic and runs locally without an LLM, graph service, or optional standards backend. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-025` | Running each read operation preserves canonical files, generated files, configuration, and persistent timestamps, including when generated state is missing or stale., Ordinary reads do not create directories, rebuild indexes on disk, install dependencies, start services, create Tasks, or publish proposals. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-026` | Stable-ID and exact-label lookup precede alias and general lexical matches; approved exact matches are not displaced by looser matches., An unknown term reports no match; an ambiguous term returns explicit alternatives with IDs and distinctions., Retrieval works without embeddings or an external semantic service. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-027` | neighbors Task returns typed relationships from the selected graph; path Task MemoryRecord returns a meaningful path within limits or explicitly reports none., A cyclic or densely connected example terminates within the configured limits and identifies any truncation; relation direction and allowed predicates are preserved., No fixed performance target or arbitrary hop count is implied; supported limits and defaults are documented. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-028` | A human or agent can distinguish ID, preferred-label, alias, lexical, or graph-traversal matches and identify their source versions., Draft and deprecated results are explicitly labeled and cannot be mistaken for currently approved definitions., Machine-readable output and concise human-facing rendering convey the same result identity and evidence. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-029` | Missing configuration, invalid modules, missing projections, stale source hashes, and an empty project extension produce specific diagnostics., Valid empty project extensions can use the imported core; stale generated data is not presented as a verified current answer., Any suggested compile or repair remains a separate explicit operation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-030` | A generated Task page explains its distinction from TRD and links to related concepts and recorded governing sources., Pages identify themselves as generated, preserve source/classification information, and direct canonical edits to their owning records., A wiki rebuild never imports hand-edited page content as canonical ontology. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-031` | A reader can start at the wiki index, find Task or a memory capability, follow a relationship, and reach its source reference., Repeated builds have stable filenames and links; validation detects broken generated internal links. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-032` | Capability-to-skill and skill-to-capability queries resolve project memory retrieval and TRD creation to their installed skill sources., The to-trd binding accurately states that creating a TRD does not create a Task., Missing or changed skill sources are reported as unavailable or stale; capability discovery invokes no skill. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-033` | Queries identify the artifacts defining a role using its actual AGENTS.md and ROLE.md pair, rather than treating Roles/INDEX.md as authority., The graph distinguishes the host Director from a confirmed Task manager and an ordinary child; ontology lookup neither assigns a role nor changes canonical role or Task state., Bindings represent selected relevant metadata without requiring a rewrite of every role, skill, or specification file. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-034` | Definition and vocabulary queries use ontology and its source references; relationships use the bounded graph; historical questions use memory., Current-authority queries read the current governing sources first; mixed queries resolve ontology terminology, retrieve memory evidence, and verify current sources when an answer concerns current behavior., A capability request returns its skill and constraints without executing the operation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-035` | Ontology publication and linking leave existing memory records byte-identical and valid under the current schema; no ontology_refs field is inserted., Memory publication or automatic capture leaves canonical ontology unchanged., Ontology setup does not broaden the memory corpus, activate a new memory backend, migrate memory, or alter its existing capture setting. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-036` | Explicit link generation creates associations only for the selected project's accessible records and resolvable concepts; memory records remain unchanged., Ambiguous or unmatched associations are identified rather than published as canonical facts., After a source record or ontology version changes, stale associations are detected; explicit rebuilding reproduces current links and does not reuse stale links as verified evidence. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-037` | A query about prior Task manager failures resolves TaskManager-related terminology and retrieves relevant existing historical memory through the supported memory interface., Expansion cannot bring excluded sources, another project's records, stale evidence, or new live records into a frozen solver context., The response identifies no matching historical evidence or unavailable memory when applicable, without inventing records or provisioning a backend. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-038` | A mixed response identifies each source type, exact concept or record identity, source version, and relevant evidence., Historical memory is not upgraded to operational authority by a concept link, and an ontology match is not presented as proof that a historical event occurred. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-039` | The current confirmed manager can freeze an explicit selected or empty packet within its granted output scope and register it through existing Task artifact/input mechanisms., The complete packet digest is held in its external artifact reference; the packet does not need a self-referential hash., Packets obey the current Task reference and artifact limits, exclude sibling drafts and prohibited sources, and introduce no Task schema field or activation route. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-040` | Each initial assignment references identical ontology packet bytes and permitted source versions., Publishing new ontology content after dispatch leaves the packet unchanged; a changed referenced file is detected and not silently substituted., Further ontology retrieval for that round is limited to its frozen content and explicitly permitted exact sources. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-041` | Ontology operations create, resume, complete, or upgrade no Task and do not alter its required team or writer., A change affecting current solver meaning is assessed by the confirmed manager and reaches affected workers only through the existing versioned input, reconciliation, review, and acceptance gates., An immaterial change retains its reason without requiring an automatic restart. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-042` | Authoritative additions originate in ONTOLOGY-depo/, SKILLS-depo/ontology/, and the affected existing reusable source collections; the Template receives them through tools/template_update.py., The update check reports the exact mapped additions and any conflicts before application; affected source/Template contracts validate after application., Only the registered Template is automatically updated; unrelated project-local installations remain unchanged. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-043` | The installed root commands resolve project sys4ai-depot and answer the initial competency questions using current root sources., Root adoption records the selected source versions and exact changed artifacts, and preserves existing memory, learning, Task, role, licensing, and independent project state., The operation does not restore an old ontology or Memory Service runtime or inherit authority from historical records. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-044` | A Template content inventory contains the reusable capability and core module but no sys4ai-depot instance data, root actor binding, memory links, generated graph/index/cache/wiki build state, or project-private source references., An empty project extension is distinguished from missing required capability. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-045` | Disposable create and first-prepare runs produce distinct project identities/namespaces and exact destination-local authority references without root project data., Setup receipts distinguish copied assets, specialized configuration, preserved content, and actual capability readiness., Initialization installs no external ontology service, RDF backend, embedding model, or product runtime. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-046` | An ordinary rerun of an earlier completed setup neither adds ontology nor relabels the project's base setup edition., A selected adoption records source/destination identity, exact module and file versions, overwrite boundaries, preserved content, and current readiness through the existing receipt/recovery model., No real existing product project receives ontology solely because this release is installed in the depot or Template. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-047` | A destination containing a customized, incomplete, or incompatible ontology package is preserved and receives precise diagnostics rather than a partial merge or false ready claim., Existing memory backend/capture settings, historical records, licenses, and bound governance remain unchanged unless the user separately selects the exact applicable change., Interrupted adoption resumes only its same recorded request and expected bytes; changed inputs or conflicting edits prevent unsafe replay. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-048` | The ontology core acceptance checks pass with no graph database, RDFLib, pySHACL, LLM, vector index, or network service available., Ontology lookup remains usable when the optional memory backend is unavailable; mixed queries report the memory limitation while retaining valid ontology results., Ordinary reads and project setup do not install or initialize optional dependencies. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-049` | A reader can resolve Task, inspect a capability, follow provenance, build the wiki explicitly, and identify the required authority for a proposed canonical edit using documented examples., Documentation distinguishes semantic retrieval from execution, generated files from authoring files, setup from operational readiness, and document approval from implementation authority., Unimplemented later features are labeled out of scope rather than advertised as available. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-050` | The initial checks cover Project and Task meaning; Task versus TRD; project memory and its authority limits; memory-retrieval capability; Task management; role source artifacts; verification versus validation; Template derivation; child-project authority; memory-publication relations; deprecated replacements; and definition provenance., Each question has an observable expected concept, relationship, distinction, source, or explicit no-result outcome; success is not defined as an LLM declaring its own answer correct., Project extensions can add competency questions without changing the shared core vocabulary. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-051` | The local automated run executes both groups, fails if either fails, and reports exact input versions and results., Negative cases cover duplicate IDs, dangling targets, label ambiguity, missing approved metadata/provenance, invalid relation types/cardinality, acyclic-relation violations, unsafe source paths, and remote JSON-LD contexts., CI invocation is documented and connected to any applicable existing pipeline; hosted CI provisioning or remote publication is not required to run these checks locally. | `active` | 0 | None |
